meta.review_notes: Re-analyzed with strict legal-safe rules. Four categories marked unknown because the privacy policy is silent on them: camera_microphone, storage_file_access, health_biometric, and childrens_data. Contact upload is described as optional in the policy text ('You can use the contact upload feature'). All claims now supported by verbatim policy excerpts.

app.name: WhatsApp Messenger
app.description: A free, end-to-end encrypted messaging and calling app used by over 2 billion people worldwide, owned by Meta.

verdict.one_liner: Your messages are encrypted, but WhatsApp shares your contacts and activity data with Meta Companies.
verdict.summary: WhatsApp states it offers end-to-end encryption and does not retain delivered messages on its servers. It also states it does not allow third-party banner ads on its Services. However, WhatsApp states that as part of the Meta Companies, it shares information with other Meta Companies, which may be used to show relevant offers and ads across Meta Company Products. It also states you may provide phone numbers from your address book on a regular basis.
verdict.recommendation_reason: WhatsApp encrypts your messages, but the policy explicitly describes sharing your contacts, device data, and activity with Meta Companies for advertising. Consider whether you are comfortable with this trade-off.

red.title: WhatsApp states you can provide phone numbers from your address book on a regular basis
red.plain_english: WhatsApp states that you can use the contact upload feature to provide phone numbers from your address book on a regular basis, including contacts who do not use WhatsApp. It claims non-user contacts cannot be identified by WhatsApp.

red.title: WhatsApp shares information with Meta Companies for ads
red.plain_english: WhatsApp states that as part of the Meta Companies, it shares information with other Meta Companies. This information may be used to show relevant offers and ads across Meta Company Products.

red.title: WhatsApp collects device identifiers linked to Meta Products
red.plain_english: WhatsApp states it collects device identifiers unique to Meta Company Products associated with the same device or account, along with hardware model, operating system, battery level, signal strength, and connection information.

red.title: WhatsApp estimates your location from your IP and phone number
red.plain_english: WhatsApp states that even if you do not use location-related features, it uses IP addresses and phone number area codes to estimate your general location.

red.title: WhatsApp does not clearly describe how to opt out of Meta sharing
red.plain_english: WhatsApp states it shares information with other Meta Companies. The policy does not clearly explain how users can opt out of this sharing while continuing to use the service.

green.title: End-to-end encryption on messages
green.plain_english: WhatsApp states it offers end-to-end encryption to protect messages against WhatsApp and third parties from reading them.

green.title: Delivered messages are deleted from servers
green.plain_english: WhatsApp states it does not retain messages in the ordinary course of providing services, and deletes them from servers once delivered.

green.title: No third-party banner ads inside the app
green.plain_english: WhatsApp states it does not allow third-party banner ads on its Services.

green.title: You can delete your account and data
green.plain_english: WhatsApp states you can delete your account, which removes account info, profile photo, group memberships, and message history.

categories.label: Camera & Microphone
categories.plain_english: The privacy policy does not clearly state whether or how WhatsApp accesses your camera or microphone.
categories.detail: The privacy policy describes messaging and calling features but does not explicitly address camera or microphone permissions. Because the policy is silent, this category is marked unknown.
concerns: Privacy policy is silent on camera and microphone access

categories.label: Location & GPS
categories.plain_english: WhatsApp states it estimates your general location from your IP address and phone number area code even if you do not use location features.
categories.detail: Precise location requires explicit user permission and is only used when you actively share your location. However, WhatsApp states it uses IP addresses and phone number area codes to estimate your general location (city and country) even without location feature use. The policy does not clearly explain how long this inferred location data is retained.
categories.policy_excerpt: Even if you do not use our location-related features, we use IP addresses and other information like phone number area codes to estimate your general location (e.g., city and country).
concerns: Passive IP-based location inference is always on with no opt-out
Policy does not clearly explain how inferred location data is used beyond diagnostics

categories.label: Contacts & Phonebook
categories.plain_english: WhatsApp states you can provide phone numbers from your address book on a regular basis, including contacts who do not use WhatsApp.
categories.detail: The policy states 'You can use the contact upload feature and provide us... with the phone numbers in your address book on a regular basis, including those of users of our Services and your other contacts.' While the policy describes this as optional, the app is designed around contact discovery. For non-users, the policy claims 'those contacts cannot be identified by us.' The policy does not clearly exclude this data from Meta-wide sharing.
categories.policy_excerpt: You can use the contact upload feature and provide us, if permitted by applicable laws, with the phone numbers in your address book on a regular basis, including those of users of our Services and your other contacts. If any of your contacts aren't yet using our Services, we'll manage this information for you in a way that ensures those contacts cannot be identified by us.
concerns: Contact data is uploaded regularly, not just once
Policy does not explicitly exclude contact data from Meta-wide data sharing
Non-user contacts are uploaded without their consent

categories.label: Storage & File Access
categories.plain_english: The privacy policy does not clearly state whether or how WhatsApp accesses your device storage or files.
categories.detail: The policy mentions media forwarding and that messages are stored on your device, but it does not explicitly address device storage or file system permissions. Because the policy is silent, this category is marked unknown.
concerns: Privacy policy is silent on device storage and file access

categories.label: Data Sharing with 3rd Parties
categories.plain_english: WhatsApp states it shares information with other Meta Companies, which may be used to show ads across Meta Company Products. It also works with third-party service providers.
categories.detail: WhatsApp states it shares information with other Meta Companies, including for 'showing relevant offers and ads across the Meta Company Products.' It also states it works with third-party service providers for infrastructure, security, and customer service, and requires them to use data on WhatsApp's behalf. The policy does not explicitly say it sells your data.
categories.policy_excerpt: As part of the Meta Companies, WhatsApp receives information from, and shares information (see here) with, the other Meta Companies. We may use the information we receive from them, and they may use the information we share with them, to help operate, provide, improve, understand, customize, support, and market our Services and their offerings, including the Meta Company Products.
concerns: Behavioral data is used to improve ad targeting on Meta platforms
Policy does not clearly describe how to opt out of Meta data sharing
Third-party service providers receive data, though with contractual restrictions

categories.label: Account & Identity Data
categories.plain_english: WhatsApp states you must provide your mobile phone number and basic information to create an account.
categories.detail: A verified mobile phone number is mandatory for account creation. The policy states you must provide 'your mobile phone number and basic information (including a profile name of your choice) to create a WhatsApp account.' Profile info is visible to other users by default. The policy does not clearly explain whether your WhatsApp account can be linked to Facebook or Instagram profiles.
categories.policy_excerpt: You must provide your mobile phone number and basic information (including a profile name of your choice) to create a WhatsApp account.
concerns: Real phone number required — no pseudonymous or anonymous use
Profile info (name, photo, last seen) is available to anyone using the Services by default

categories.label: Behavioural & Ad Tracking
categories.plain_english: WhatsApp states it collects information about how you use its Services and shares it with Meta Companies, which may use it to show ads across Meta Company Products.
categories.detail: The policy states it collects 'information about your activity (including how you use our Services, your Services settings, how you interact with others using our Services... and the time, frequency, and duration of your activities and interactions).' It also states this information is shared with Meta Companies and may be used for 'showing relevant offers and ads across the Meta Company Products.' The policy does not mention an opt-out for non-EU/UK users.
categories.policy_excerpt: We collect information about your activity on our Services, like service-related, diagnostic, and performance information. This includes information about your activity (including how you use our Services, your Services settings, how you interact with others using our Services (including when you interact with a business), and the time, frequency, and duration of your activities and interactions).
concerns: Behavioral data is shared with Meta Companies for ad targeting
Policy does not clearly describe how to opt out of this tracking

categories.label: Children's Data Handling
categories.plain_english: The privacy policy does not clearly state age requirements or how children's data is handled.
categories.detail: The privacy policy text analyzed does not mention age requirements, children, or child-specific data protections. Because the policy is silent, this category is marked unknown.
concerns: Privacy policy is silent on age requirements and children's data

categories.label: Network & Internet Activity
categories.plain_english: WhatsApp states it collects your IP address and connection information, and uses your IP to estimate your general location.
categories.detail: The policy states it collects 'IP address, device operations information, and identifiers' as part of device and connection information. It also states it uses 'IP addresses and other information like phone number area codes to estimate your general location.' Connection metadata (online status, last seen) is collected and shared with contacts per account settings.
categories.policy_excerpt: We collect device and connection-specific information when you install, access, or use our Services. This includes information such as hardware model, operating system information, battery level, signal strength, app version, browser information, mobile network, connection information (including phone number, mobile operator or ISP), language and time zone, IP address, device operations information, and identifiers.
concerns: IP-based location inference is always on with no opt-out
Connection metadata is collected and shared with contacts

categories.label: Device Info & Fingerprinting
categories.plain_english: WhatsApp states it collects detailed device information, including identifiers unique to Meta Company Products associated with the same device or account.
categories.detail: The policy enumerates an extensive list of device data: 'hardware model, operating system information, battery level, signal strength, app version, browser information, mobile network, connection information (including phone number, mobile operator or ISP), language and time zone, IP address, device operations information, and identifiers (including identifiers unique to Meta Company Products associated with the same device or account).' This explicitly enables cross-app device linking across the Meta ecosystem.
categories.policy_excerpt: We collect device and connection-specific information when you install, access, or use our Services. This includes information such as hardware model, operating system information, battery level, signal strength, app version, browser information, mobile network, connection information (including phone number, mobile operator or ISP), language and time zone, IP address, device operations information, and identifiers (including identifiers unique to Meta Company Products associated with the same device or account).
concerns: Device identifiers explicitly linked across Meta products
Battery level and signal strength collection goes beyond what is clearly needed for service operation

categories.label: Health & Biometric Data
categories.plain_english: The privacy policy does not clearly state whether WhatsApp collects health or biometric data.
categories.detail: The privacy policy does not mention health or biometric data. Because the policy is silent, this category is marked unknown. Any biometric authentication (Face ID, Touch ID) is handled at the operating system level.
concerns: Privacy policy is silent on health and biometric data

categories.label: Financial & Payment Data
categories.plain_english: WhatsApp states it collects payment and transaction information only if you use its payments services.
categories.detail: Payment services are an optional feature available in select markets. If used, the policy states that 'we process additional information about you, including payment account and transaction information.' The policy defers detailed payment privacy practices to a separate payments privacy policy, which was not reviewed in this analysis.
categories.policy_excerpt: If you use our payments services, or use our Services meant for purchases or other financial transactions, we process additional information about you, including payment account and transaction information.
concerns: Separate payments privacy policy not analyzed — full practices unknown
Payment data collection and retention practices not fully disclosed in main policy

categories.label: Data Deletion & User Rights
categories.plain_english: WhatsApp states you can delete your account, which removes account data and undelivered messages from its servers. Some data may be retained for legal and security purposes.
categories.detail: WhatsApp provides an in-app 'Delete My Account' feature and a 'Request Account Info' feature for data portability. However, the policy states that 'We store information for as long as necessary for the purposes identified in this Privacy Policy, including to provide our Services or for other legitimate purposes, such as complying with legal obligations, enforcing and preventing violations of our Terms, or protecting or defending our rights, property, and users.' Account deletion does not affect data held by other users.
categories.policy_excerpt: When you delete your WhatsApp account, your undelivered messages are deleted from our servers as well as any of your other information we no longer need to operate and provide our Services. Deleting your account will, for example, delete your account info and profile photo, delete you from all WhatsApp groups, and delete your WhatsApp message history.
concerns: Data held by other users (screenshots, message copies) is not deletable
Some retention for legal/security purposes is not time-limited in the policy
Uninstalling without using 'Delete Account' does not delete server-side data

categories.label: Policy Change Notification
categories.plain_english: WhatsApp states it may amend its Privacy Policy and will provide notice 'as appropriate.' The policy does not clearly explain what happens if you disagree with changes.
categories.detail: The policy states: We may amend or update our Privacy Policy. We will provide you notice of amendments to this Privacy Policy, as appropriate, and update the Effective Date at the top of this Privacy Policy. It does not explain what as appropriate means, nor does it describe any mechanism for rejecting changes or the consequences of continuing to use the service after changes.
categories.policy_excerpt: We may amend or update our Privacy Policy. We will provide you notice of amendments to this Privacy Policy, as appropriate, and update the "Effective Date" at the top of this Privacy Policy. Please review our Privacy Policy from time to time.
concerns: Notice is provided 'as appropriate' — not guaranteed for all changes
Policy does not explain how to reject changes or what happens if you disagree
